thread.content: The UI so far looks like garbage. And I think right now it might have issues preventing it from rendering at all (just seeing white). But even before that it looked bad. Remember the goal is to have visually stunning, unique, award-winning designs for each page

mutations.rationale: User explicitly flagged 'might have issues preventing it from rendering at all (just seeing white)'. Nothing else in this initiative matters until the app renders. Tagged P1 and S so it gets picked up immediately.

item.name: command-center-render-triage
item.title: Diagnose and fix command-center white-screen / render regression
item.description: User reports the command-center UI may currently render as a blank white screen. Reproduce the failure (browser devtools console, network tab, vite build output), identify the root cause (likely candidates: missing route component, broken import, R3F/Three.js init crash, CSS that hides content, or a runtime error in one of the 6 page components), and ship a fix. Acceptance: every route under /mission-control, /hive, /forge, /ledger, /broadcast, /panorama renders non-empty content with no console errors in a fresh browser session, both in `vrooli scenario start command-center` dev mode and in a vite production build. Add a smoke test (Playwright or equivalent) that loads each route and asserts non-blank content so this regression cannot silently recur.

mutations.rationale: The current architecture research is structural (R3F + CSS vars + Recharts). 'Award-winning' is a visual-language problem, not an architecture problem — without a concrete reference brief, the theming-engine work will keep producing competent-but-generic output.

item.name: command-center-visual-design-references
item.title: Curate visual references and design language for award-winning dashboards
item.description: Compile a concrete reference deck for each of the 6 themes (Ground Control, Bioluminescent, Foundry, Vault, Signal Tower, Cosmos) drawing from Awwwards/FWA/CSSDA dashboard winners, sci-fi UI work (Territory Studio: Blade Runner 2049, The Martian, Oblivion), generative-art studios (Active Theory, Resn, Hello Monday), and data-viz showcases (Pitch Interactive, Stamen). Output: a markdown brief per theme with 5–10 reference images/links, a typography pairing, a color/material palette beyond CSS variables (gradients, noise, glass, glow, grain), motion principles, and a 'one signature hero element' that makes the page memorable. This brief becomes the visual spec the theming-engine and per-page work executes against.

mutations.rationale: User said even before the render bug it 'looked bad'. The existing theming-engine item builds the system; this item is the actual aesthetic execution against that system. Splitting the two prevents 'theming engine works = visual goal achieved' false-completion.

item.name: command-center-visual-polish-pass
item.title: Visual elevation pass: take all 6 pages from functional to award-winning
item.description: After the theming engine and kiosk UX land, do a dedicated quality pass that pushes each of the 6 pages to portfolio-grade. Per page: implement the signature hero element from the references brief, add layered depth (R3F scene + foreground UI + grain/glass overlays), tune typography (variable fonts, optical sizing, generous tracking for kiosk distance), add micro-motion (number tickers, ambient particle drift, hover/focus states even though kiosk has no hover — use auto-cycle highlights instead), ensure every panel has intentional negative space, and remove anything that looks like a default Recharts/MUI/Tailwind look. Acceptance: side-by-side compare each page against its references brief; an unbiased reviewer would call the result 'designed' rather than 'styled'. Capture before/after screenshots in the item folder.

mutations.rationale: Per-page visual identity is the stated differentiator of the entire initiative; bumping from P2 to P1 reflects that and gets it queued right after the render fix.

Existing item description risks being interpreted as 'wire up CSS variables and ship'. User feedback makes clear that bar is too low; appending the explicit quality criteria keeps the item honest without rewriting it.

proposal.rationale: Address the user's two concerns: triage the white-screen render regression as urgent blocking work, and raise the visual-quality bar with a dedicated design-elevation item plus a references study, since the existing theming-engine item is scaffolding-level and won't on its own produce award-winning results.
